clue.text: Quite a character, Fred, in The Gate of Angels

definitions.meaning: quite in the sense of reasonably or moderately

definitions.text: a character, Fred, in The Gate of Angels
definitions.meaning: Fred is the hero of Penelope Fitzgerald's novel The Gate of Angels, a young Cambridge fellow

explanation.surface: A remark that Fred in Penelope Fitzgerald's novel is quite a character.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Quite a character' one phrase; split it, and 'Quite' is an adverb on its own while the rest names the hero's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite and the adverb both mean reasonably or to a moderate degree; the novel's hero is Fred Fairly.

clue.text: Role of The Third Man's author

definitions.meaning: third man is a cricket position, so his job on the field is this
Henry ..., the eighteenth-century writer of Tom Jones

explanation.surface: A question about the part played by the writer of The Third Man.
explanation.walkthrough: The Third Man suggests the Graham Greene film, but third man is a fielding position in cricket, near the boundary behind the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Third man is a cricket fielding position, and Henry Fielding wrote Tom Jones.

clue.text: One cat almost swallowing upper-class Trojan spokesman

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the shortened cat swallows, that is takes inside, the next piece
almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: a lioness is a big cat

explanation.surface: A single cat gulps down a posh Trojan.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Aeneid Ilioneus is the Trojan who speaks for Aeneas' men before Dido and later King Latinus.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil gives Ilioneus the role of the Trojans' envoy and orator in the Aeneid.

clue.text: Spy writer's play oddly vanished completely

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first and third, have vanished from the word play

parts.note: all means wholly or completely

explanation.surface: A spy novelist's play disappeared without trace.
explanation.walkthrough: Gavin Lyall was an English writer of spy and thriller novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Gavin Lyall wrote spy thrillers such as the Major Maxim series.

clue.text: Book by David Lodge that's well done!

definitions.meaning: Lodge's 1988 novel about an academic shadowing a factory manager
an exclamation of praise for a job done skilfully

explanation.surface: Praise for one of David Lodge's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation praising a skilful job is also the title of Lodge's industrial campus novel.

clue.text: Philosopher's tune a milkman played

indicators.note: played as in played around with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A philosopher's favourite tune, performed by a milkman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' looks like music but is the anagram signal for TUNE A MILKMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanuel Kant was the German philosopher of the Critique of Pure Reason.

clue.text: Longfellow's work does better with island men

parts.note: to excel is to do better than others
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Longfellow's writing outdoes islanders.
explanation.walkthrough: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers, a crossword convention for men.
explanation.definitionFit: Excelsior is Longfellow's 1841 poem about a youth climbing an Alpine pass.

clue.text: Work a playwright left unfinished somewhere in Iberia

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the playwright's name is left without its final letter

parts.note: Joe Orton, the English writer of Loot and Entertaining Mr Sloane

explanation.surface: A dramatist's work left uncompleted somewhere in Spain or Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: Orton fits the surface twice: he was murdered in 1967, leaving his last play unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the English name for Porto, the Portuguese port city on the Douro.

clue.text: King items rewritten in a musical

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters of the word are written out in a new order

explanation.surface: A king's possessions reworked in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: Kismet is the 1953 Broadway musical set in old Baghdad.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is a 1953 Broadway show with music adapted from Borodin.

clue.text: Prophet, priest, judge, and a Hebrew leader

parts.note: Eli is the priest of Shiloh in the Book of Samuel, a crossword stock priest

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the front of Hebrew is wanted

explanation.surface: A list of the roles of an Old Testament leader: prophet, priest and judge.
explanation.walkthrough: The list looks like a description of one man, but only 'Prophet' defines; 'priest', 'judge', 'a' and 'Hebrew leader' build the name piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is the Old Testament prophet who confronted Ahab and was taken up in a whirlwind.

clue.text: Tiny distances taken by love letters to Aspasia

indicators.note: the tiny distances are taken by love, so love comes first and the distances follow it

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, so O
a micron is a millionth of a metre

explanation.surface: Love letters sent to Aspasia, the companion of Pericles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love letters' reads as one phrase; split after 'love'. Aspasia was a Greek woman of classical Athens, so 'letters to Aspasia' means letters of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Omicron is a letter of the Greek alphabet, the alphabet Aspasia of Athens would have read.

clue.text: Murderer outside a gym toilet in bad, vacuous, Sabatini novel

indicators.note: the murderer's name goes outside, around the next two pieces

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
PT is physical training, the school gym lesson

indicators.note: the toilet goes in the emptied word for bad
vacuous means empty, so the word bad keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: loo is a British word for a toilet

explanation.surface: A murderer stalks a gym and its toilet in a bad, empty-headed novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Blood is Rafael Sabatini's 1922 pirate adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabatini's 1922 swashbuckler follows a doctor turned pirate, Peter Blood.

clue.text: Prince of Scotland put on trendy clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the two outer pieces dress or wrap around the Gaelic name

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on
in means fashionable
Alba is the Gaelic name for Scotland

explanation.surface: A Scottish prince dresses in fashionable clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like a noun but is the verb, and 'of' is a link. Donalbain is Duncan's younger son in Macbeth, who flees to Ireland after the murder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Macbeth Donalbain is a son of King Duncan, so a royal heir of Scotland.

clue.text: Forgetfulness and an article on its French equivalent

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another is written after it

parts.note: le is the French definite article, the equivalent of the English one
the definite article in English

explanation.surface: A grammar note comparing an English article with its French counterpart.
explanation.walkthrough: Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the dead drank from the river Lethe to lose all memory, so the name means oblivion.

clue.text: The nurse in a novel with a nervous debility

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A nurse in a novel who suffers from her nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal: THE NURSE IN A rearranged gives NEURASTHENI, and 'with a' adds the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurasthenia was the Victorian diagnosis for nervous exhaustion and weakness.

clue.text: A survey about Italy's capital by a wife of Corleone

parts.note: a poll is a survey of opinion
on means about, concerning

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, so just the front of Italy's

explanation.surface: A survey about Rome's region by a Mafia don's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Godfather Michael Corleone marries Apollonia while hiding in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollonia Vitelli is the Sicilian bride of Michael Corleone in The Godfather.

clue.text: Daughter of a king or duke, grabbed by Charlie Lamb

indicators.note: the pieces in the middle are grabbed, that is held, by the outer ones

parts.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A princess or duchess seized by Charles Lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie Lamb' reads as one person, Charles Lamb, but splits: C from the radio alphabet, then ELIA, Lamb's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordelia is King Lear's youngest and faithful daughter in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Bad, certain to be reported, tale of houseboat dwellers

parts.note: off means gone bad, like sour milk

indicators.note: to be reported means a word is heard in speech rather than seen

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A grim story, sure to be told, about people on houseboats.
explanation.walkthrough: Offshore is Penelope Fitzgerald's Booker-winning novel about houseboat dwellers on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope Fitzgerald's 1979 Booker winner follows people living on boats moored at Battersea Reach.

clue.text: Synthetic fir bark fools an actor

indicators.note: synthetic means artificially made up, so the letters are made up into a new order

explanation.surface: Artificial fir bark is used to trick someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of FIR BARK FOOLS gives the stage name of the horror actor who played Frankenstein's monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Karloff was the English film star of Frankenstein and other horror films.

clue.text: Would-be poet's resistance song, docked by the late queen

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: docked means cut short, losing its last letter, like a docked tail

parts.note: a hymn is a song of praise
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A wannabe poet's protest song cut short by the late Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resistance song' suggests a protest song, but it splits into R and HYMN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymer is a mere versifier, someone writing verse who falls short of true poetry.

clue.text: Right-leaning European, ousting a new conservative

indicators.note: the conservative ousts, that is replaces, the letters for a new

parts.note: an Italian is a European

explanation.surface: A European rightist who displaces a new Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a new' gives A and N, the letters that leave ITALIAN. 'Right-leaning' sounds political but describes letters that slope to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right, so it literally leans that way.

clue.text: Book somewhere to stay

definitions.meaning: Arthur Hailey's 1965 novel set in a New Orleans establishment
a place offering rooms to travellers

explanation.surface: Reserve a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' reads as the verb reserve, but it is a noun: the title of Arthur Hailey's bestselling novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest house with rooms for travellers is somewhere to stay, and Hailey's novel bears that one-word title.

clue.text: Stays to welcome old lover, returning in good faith

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the remaining pieces go inside

parts.note: to bide is to stay or remain

indicators.note: returning means the word for lover is read backwards

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast or lover of something

explanation.surface: Someone remains loyal to an old flame who comes back, trusting them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old lover' looks like an ex, but splits into two pieces; 'returning' turns only the lover. 'in' is a link, and the Latin phrase means good faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is the legal term for honest intention, sincerity of purpose.

clue.text: Dramatist penning a note for another

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the playwright wraps round the letter

parts.note: Christopher Fry, the verse dramatist of The Lady's Not for Burning

explanation.surface: A playwright writing a note for a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: The first dramatist builds the wordplay; 'another' is the definition, a second dramatist, Michael Frayn, author of Noises Off and Copenhagen.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Frayn is a fellow English dramatist, so another of the same calling as Fry.

clue.text: Pigment covering over Hippomenes

indicators.note: the pigment covers, that is surrounds, the letter for over

parts.note: melanin is the dark pigment of skin and hair
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Paint applied over a figure from Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: Hippomenes, who won Atalanta by dropping golden apples in their race, is called by another name in some versions of the myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid calls Atalanta's suitor Hippomenes, while other sources name the same racer Melanion or Milanion.

clue.text: Impudence the mother of Epaphus shows Seneca's brother

parts.note: gall is cheek or impudence
Io, loved by Zeus and turned into a heifer, bore him Epaphus

explanation.surface: A myth figure shows impudence to a Roman philosopher's brother.
explanation.walkthrough: Gallio, the brother of the philosopher Seneca, was the Roman governor before whom Paul was brought in Acts 18.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucius Junius Gallio was the elder brother of Seneca the Younger and proconsul of Achaea.

clue.text: Billy Bunter author recalled teacher eating veg

indicators.note: the reversed teacher eats, that is swallows, the vegetable
recalled is read as called back, so the word for teacher runs backwards

parts.note: sir is what schoolchildren call a male teacher
chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: Billy Bunter's creator remembers a schoolmaster munching vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is the greedy schoolboy of Greyfriars, written by Charles Hamilton under the pen name Frank Richards; a teacher eating fits the school story.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Richards was the pen name under which Charles Hamilton wrote the Greyfriars stories about Billy Bunter.

clue.text: Box of letters from Seneca

indicators.note: the letters taken from the name are used in a new order

explanation.surface: A box containing letters written by Seneca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' is a verb, and 'letters from Seneca' recalls his famous moral epistles, but means only the letters of his name rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To box something is to enclose it in a case or container.
